subject: research/accel-nsgatune
professional: an evolutionary multi-objective optimisation researcher who reviews NSGA-II parameter studies for IEEE TEVC or the EMO conference, checking first: is the ground truth right, are differences between settings tested (Mann-Whitney/Wilcoxon with a multiple-comparison correction, or CIs on the mean), was tuning done on held-out seeds or instances (irace-style), does the study vary the budget, and how the defaults compare with the standard guidance (per-gene mutation 1/n)

evidence.correctness: Independent script scratchpad/accel-nsgatune/indep.py rebuilds the 3,840-design space from the raw data files only (accel-kws results.json, accel-codesign datapath_area.json) and accel-nsga's stated equations, without importing the author's search code: exact fronts of 41 (50 us) and 33 (200 us) distinct objective vectors, matching results.txt; true-front normalised hypervolume by coordinate-compression grid 0.703466 and 0.705348, equal to the author's objective_hv to 6 d.p. (Monte Carlo 400k points 0.70358/0.70544). Random-search baseline has a closed form: every front signature is a single gene, so E[share] = 400/3840 = 0.1042 at both deadlines; the author's 30 seeds give 0.129 and 0.116 (reproduced exactly), 1,000 fresh seeds give 0.1033 and 0.1040, so the 50 us baseline in the README is a seed draw 2.9 SE above its expectation (direction makes the NSGA-II margin look smaller, not larger). Reproduced pop 10 mut 0.02 rows exactly (0.398, 0.773). Held-out seeds (60 fresh seeds per config, scratchpad/accel-nsgatune/heldout.py) confirm the qualitative findings: pop 20 mut 0.25 0.286/0.564 vs mut 0.02-0.1 0.380-0.392/0.717-0.764; 'best at 200 us' flips from mut 0.02 (0.746) to 0.05 (0.764), as the limitations section anticipates.
evidence.completeness: Claimed: a 4 x 5 population x mutation sweep with crossover, a no-crossover variant at pop 20 and 40, both deadlines, 30 seeds, results.json/results.txt, figure, 4 tests, live page. All present and runnable: tests 4/4 pass in 0.04 s; results.txt has all 62 rows; figure.py reads the '== front found by mutation rate' block; research homepage builder (research/_homepage/build.py --out scratch) renders accel-nsgatune/index.html with the summary, '4 tests' and mutation_sweep.svg. No TODOs or stubs. Next steps (budget sweep, larger space) are stated as future, not done.
evidence.verification: `cd research/accel-nsgatune && python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v`: 4 tests OK. Six mutants via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: 4 caught, all on the crossover path, by test_matches_reference_nsga2_with_crossover (bit-for-bit equality with accel-nsga's nsga2 on seed 5): crossover gate inverted, mutation halved, truncation to the worst instead of best, tournament picking the loser. 2 SURVIVED: forcing crossover=True (the no-crossover switch, the only new code, is ignored) and replacing the exact-front intersection score in run.py with a count of found front points. test_no_crossover_child_is_copy_when_no_mutation (tests/test_tune.py:20) asserts only len >= 10, not that children are copies. The scoring and the experiment driver have no test.
evidence.craft: Read tune.py (30 lines), tests/test_tune.py, experiments/run.py, figure.py, and accel-nsga/src/accel_nsga/search.py (176 lines) that it imports. Small, deterministic, stdlib only, seeds explicit. Defects: nsga2_x is a copy of accel-nsga's nsga2 loop with one changed line rather than a flag added upstream (copied engine, kept in sync only by the equality test); the no-crossover branch still draws an unused second tournament winner b; imports by sys.path insertion of a sibling project; per-gene mutation resamples uniformly including the current value, so effective rate is about 0.83 x nominal on dims (40, 6, 4, 4), undisclosed. Acceptable to a senior reviewer with those noted.
evidence.claims: Checked against results.txt and Welch t on the stored mean/sd (n=30): table rows (0.282/0.587, 0.386/0.705, 0.398/0.773, 0.399/0.759, 0.178/0.297, 0.132/0.185, 0.450/0.731) all match (pass); 'pop 80 is 20% of the budget' 80/400 (pass); hypervolume 0.97-0.998 and slightly higher at high mutation (pass). Fail: homepage summary 'Removing crossover changes little' (research/_homepage/projects.json:2821) and README headline 'Crossover matters little' (README.md:38): at 200 us pop 40 mut 0.1 crossover finds 0.663 vs 0.486 without (Welch t = 6.2; held-out 0.676 vs 0.529), and at 50 us pop 20 mut 0.02 no-crossover is better, 0.450 vs 0.388 (t = 2.9; held-out 0.428 vs 0.380); crossover's effect is sign-changing and sizeable, not small. 'Level with or slightly ahead at every mutation rate' at 50 us holds for pop 20 only (pop 40 mut 0.05: 0.328 vs 0.363). 'Below about 0.1 mutation the curve is flat ... within about one seed sd' (README.md:37) compares differences of 30-seed means with the per-seed sd: pop 10, 200 us, 0.773 vs 0.725 is t = 3.3. Limitations (one budget, tuned on the reported score, stylised models, no CIs) are stated on the README and the page summary. AI-assistance and no-affiliation statements present.
evidence.fitness: A researcher building on accel-nsga can: everything reproduces from stdlib in minutes against an exact front, and the main finding (accel-nsga's mutation 0.25 was too high for a 400-design budget; low mutation and small populations find about 0.38/0.75 of the front) survives held-out seeds. Nearest prior work: Deb et al. 2002 (cited) and its standard per-gene mutation 1/n, which for 4 genes is exactly accel-nsga's 0.25, not mentioned; parameter-tuning studies for EAs (Eiben and Smit 2011, Swarm Evol. Comput.; irace, Lopez-Ibanez et al. 2016) not cited. Result is sound but incremental: that a small budget favours exploitation (low mutation, small populations) on a 4-gene discrete space is the expected outcome, not new; it is a useful internal correction to accel-nsga, not a publishable result on its own.
evidence.domain: Against EMO practice for parameter studies: exact ground-truth front and a share-of-front metric beside hypervolume (good, and it shows HV is uninformative here); common seeds across configs. Departs: no significance tests or CIs and no multiple-comparison control across 62 configurations, differences judged by per-seed sd; tuning and reporting on the same seeds (acknowledged); a single budget, so the 'small population wins' claim is confounded with budget (acknowledged); mutation operator's effective rate below nominal; no comparison with the 1/n default rationale. A reviewer would accept the direction of the mutation finding and ask for tests, a held-out seed set and a budget sweep before the crossover conclusions.

defects.what: The page summary 'Removing crossover changes little' and README headline 'Crossover matters little' are contradicted by the project's own numbers: at 200 us pop 40 mut 0.1 crossover finds 0.663 vs 0.486 without (Welch t = 6.2; held-out seeds 0.676 vs 0.529), and at 50 us pop 20 mut 0.02 removing crossover helps, 0.450 vs 0.388 (t = 2.9). Crossover's effect is sizeable and changes sign with deadline and mutation rate.

Differences between 30-seed means are judged against the per-seed sd ('within about one seed sd', 'one to two seed sd'), not the standard error; no significance tests, CIs or multiple-comparison control over 62 configurations. The 'curve is flat below 0.1' claim fails a t-test (pop 10, 200 us, 0.773 vs 0.725, t = 3.3).

The only new code, the no-crossover switch, is untested: forcing crossover=True leaves all 4 tests green; test_no_crossover_child_is_copy_when_no_mutation asserts only len >= 10, not that children are copies. The exact-front score in run.py has no test (replacing the intersection with a count survives).

Random-search baseline reported as 0.129 (50 us) without noting its closed-form expectation 400/3840 = 0.104 (every front signature is a single gene); the 30-seed draw is 2.9 SE high (1,000 seeds: 0.1033).

Prior work not engaged: the 'untuned' mutation 0.25 is the standard per-gene 1/n default for 4 genes (Deb), and EA parameter-tuning literature (Eiben and Smit 2011; irace, Lopez-Ibanez et al. 2016) is not cited; the low-mutation/small-population result at a small budget is the expected outcome, so novelty is internal to accel-nsga.

Per-gene mutation resamples uniformly including the current value, so the effective mutation rate is about 0.83 x the nominal one on dims (40, 6, 4, 4) (0.975, 0.833, 0.75, 0.75); reported rates are nominal and this is not disclosed.

'At 50 us the mutation-only variant is level with or slightly ahead of NSGA-II at every mutation rate' holds for population 20 only; at population 40 it is behind at mutation 0.05 (0.328 vs 0.363) and 0.1 (0.307 vs 0.319).

nsga2_x copies accel-nsga's nsga2 loop with one line changed instead of adding the switch upstream; the no-crossover branch draws an unused second tournament winner; imports by sys.path insertion of a sibling project.

verdict: A small, honest and reproducible follow-up whose numbers are right and whose main finding holds, but whose crossover conclusion is stated more weakly than its own data allow and whose new code path is untested. Independently rebuilt from the raw data files, the exact fronts (41 and 33 designs) and the true-front hypervolumes (0.703466, 0.705348) match to six decimals; rows reproduce exactly; and on 60 held-out seeds the headline survives: accel-nsga's mutation 0.25 finds 0.29/0.56 of the front at 400 designs, mutation 0.02-0.1 finds 0.38-0.39/0.72-0.76. Weaknesses: 'removing crossover changes little' on the page is contradicted by gaps of 0.15-0.18 (t = 6) at 200 us and a reversal at 50 us; differences are judged against per-seed sd rather than standard errors, with no tests across 62 configurations; the random baseline 0.129 is a seed draw above its closed form 0.104; the no-crossover switch and the scoring survive seeded mutants; prior tuning literature and the 1/n default are not engaged, and the result is incremental. Does not meet the bar (claims 2, verification 2); finished (completeness 3).
